faithful_mappings: Standing Committee of the National People's Congress
explanation: President corresponds to country president: In the political system of Russia, the president is the highest head of state and government. In the political system of China, the country president is also the highest head of state. This mapping represents the highest leader in the two political systems.

Federal parliament corresponds to National People's Representative Meeting: In the political system of Russia, the federal parliament is the highest legislative body. In the political system of China, the National People's Representative Meeting is also the highest legislative body. This mapping represents the highest legislative body in the two political systems.

State Duma corresponds to the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress: In the political system of Russia, the State Duma is a part of the Federal Parliament and is responsible for reviewing and passing laws. In the political system of China, the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress is a permanent institution of the National People's Representative Meeting and is responsible for legislative work during the National People's Congress's recess. This mapping represents the legislative bodies in the two political systems.

background.source: The Russian Political System is a federal semi-presidential republic, as stipulated by the Constitution of Russia. The President serves as the head of state, while the Prime Minister, who is appointed by the President with parliament's approval, heads a multi-party system with executive power. The two houses of the Federal Assembly are in charge of legislative power, and the President and government provide legislatively binding by-laws. Though Russia has encountered significant challenges in establishing a post-Soviet political system, the adoption of a new constitution in 1993 creating a strong presidency ushered in a period of stabilization. Putin's government implemented reforms to strengthen federal control, including rolling back the power of the regions.
background.target: The Chinese Political System is a socialist republic with a one-party dictatorship led by the Chinese Communist Party (CCP). The country is headed by a general secretary who is typically the paramount leader. Unlike many other countries, China does not hold any direct elections at the national level. The State power in China is vested in the CCP, the State Council, and its provincial and local representation. The State uses internal references to maintain control and keep its cadres up to date with the latest developments within the country. China has 22 provinces, 4 directly administered municipalities, and 5 autonomous regions. The political system in China is highly authoritarian, with political opposition, dissent, and civil rights being curtailed. Elections are held at the local level only and are fiercely restricted by government censorship and interference. The National People's Representative Meeting and the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress oversee the country's legislature.
